B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Miro says MCP is available across plans without a separate MCP price; each plan has a daily call allowance. Enterprise availability requires admin enablement. The linked Miro subscription is separately priced.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Free plan is available; Starter, Business, and Enterprise are offered. The captured official pricing page describes paid plans as per-seat but did not provide stable numeric amounts in the extracted evidence; Enterprise is custom priced.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Daily MCP calls: Free 100, Starter 500, Business 2,000, Enterprise 10,000. Limits reset at 00:00 UTC. Calls are counted regardless of AI credit use. Calls are blocked after the allowance until reset; the error prompts an upgrade. Enterprise customers may request higher limits. Miro subscriptions are per seat; AI credits are separate and plan-dependent.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Enterprise admins enable MCP at organization level and select all or specific teams; it may be disabled by default. Access follows the authorized user's existing Miro board permissions. The connection is documented as one team per user at a time across clients; authorizing a different team or client supersedes the previous connection. OAuth team selection is required.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls plan allowances and endpoint behavior; organization admins control Enterprise MCP enablement and team selection; the user authorizes a team and their existing Miro permissions constrain access.

The endpoint returns HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.miro.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` and body `{"error":"Authentication required"}`. Protected-resource metadata: `resource=https://mcp.miro.com/`; `authorization_servers=[https://mcp.miro.com/]`; `scopes_supported=[boards:read, boards:write, openid, email]`; `bearer_methods_supported=[header]`. Authorization-server metadata: issuer `https://mcp.miro.com/`, authorization endpoint `/authorize`, token endpoint `/token`, registration endpoint `/register`, `response_types_supported=[code]`, `grant_types_supported=[authorization_code, refresh_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer]`, token auth methods `[client_secret_post, client_secret_basic]`, PKCE `[S256]`, grant profile `[urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-profile:id-jag]`. OIDC configuration additionally reports token endpoint auth `[none]`, revocation endpoint `/oidc/revoke`, audience `https://mcp.miro.com`, and ID-token signing algorithm `[HS256]`. Token lifetime is NOT FOUND. Miro documentation calls the flow OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and describes signed OIDC ID tokens with verified email.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official list labels tools Search/Read or Write/Update, but no readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint values are published. Canvas update is documented as creating, updating, and deleting items; separate code-widget deletion is documented in a changelog. 2. The changelog says board_create requires user confirmation; canvas deletion is described as explicit and consent-gated. These are documented safeguards, but server enforcement is not established. FAQ says human-in-the-loop confirmation details are evolving. 3. OAuth scopes are boards:read, boards:write, openid, email. Existing Miro board permissions apply; Enterprise admins enable MCP organization-wide or for selected teams. OAuth team connection is 1:1 per user across clients. Redirect URI approval and token lifetime are not documented; metadata advertises revocation endpoint /oidc/revoke. 4. No read-only mode or tool filter documented. User selects one team; Enterprise admins can choose org-wide or selected-team access. No alternate official endpoint documented. 5. Docs say current permissions govern access; no MCP-specific field masking or PII exclusion documented. 6. Daily quotas are 100/500/2,000/10,000 calls by Free/Starter/Business/Enterprise; reset 00:00 UTC; further calls blocked. Enterprise can request increases. Large canvas reads may be expensive; docs recommend scoping to a frame. 7. Server-side schema validation, coercion, argument correction, and operator overrides are Unknown. 8. Enterprise usage is visible to admins; request-level audit details are described as evolving. Telemetry and opt-out are Unknown. 9. No feedback/rating tool appears in the reviewed official list. The usage-limit error prompts an upgrade; docs pages include feedback forms and bug-report links. 10. Server tools provide canvas composition and format skills. Separate official client repository distributes additional skills. The official reference recommends loading composer guidance once before writing and format guidance as needed; enforcement is not documented. 11. OAuth team selection changes the active team connection; the previous connection is superseded. Other effects of past agent behavior on outputs/tools/resources are Unknown. 12. No nested server or proxy hierarchy documented. Team selection is stateful but the documented tool interface is a single hosted server. 13. No arbitrary raw API request, SQL, or script execution tool documented.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server is closed source and no complete verbatim tools/list schemas or initialize instructions were available. The public repository is a client-integration/skills repository, not code for the deployed endpoint, so a token estimate cannot be calculated from it.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The documented MCP abstraction does not expose the full REST API. Miro states REST API access includes team, organization, and project data on Enterprise and webhooks, while MCP docs describe a curated subset of board operations. The REST API covers items and operations not currently represented in the MCP tool list, including connectors, tags, and broader team/org/project operations. See Miro's comparison and FAQ for current limitations.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The reference instructs agents to load the canvas spec once before writing, load format-specific guidance on top of it, search before reading, and use SVG diffs. Miro says these tools guide agent behavior, but hosted enforcement of ordering is not shown. The public integration repository includes additional client-side skills.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Miro states that permissions respect existing board access controls and that current user permissions govern access. OAuth/OIDC documentation describes signed ID tokens with verified email. Daily MCP calls are capped by plan and reset at 00:00 UTC. Miro's general security page says data is encrypted in transit and at rest and not used to train Miro AI models; the latter is a product-wide statement, not an MCP-specific term found in the captured MCP docs.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Miro describes the hosted MCP server as available across plans, connecting AI clients to boards, and respecting the user's existing Miro permissions. The usage page says calls beyond the daily allowance are blocked until reset.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance and daily call blocking are documented as server/product behavior. Admin enablement and team selection are described in setup documentation. Request-level audit behavior, telemetry, masking, retention, and exact confirmation enforcement are not established by the reviewed evidence. General security and AI-training claims are vendor documentation; implementation details for the hosted MCP server were not public.

contradictions: The input endpoint is https://mcp.miro.com/mcp, while current setup guides tell clients to connect to https://mcp.miro.com/. The input path returns 401 and has its own protected-resource metadata; documentation does not explain the path difference.

OAuth metadata advertises boards:write, while the official tool reference classifies multiple operations as Write/Update; no scope-to-tool mapping is published, so the breadth of write authority cannot be inferred from the tool list.

The official tool reference gives 20 current names, while the official changelog separately documents five code_widget_* names absent from that reference. Current availability of those five is therefore uncertain.

Claude's Anthropic-verified connector directory states 31 tools but its captured text shows 24 names, including eight legacy names Miro says have been removed. It does not expose seven names in the captured page text, and its visible listing lacks current canvas/prototype tools.
observations_for_research: The server exposes bulk canvas editing through SVG; the official documentation says a single diff operation can create, update, and delete board items, rather than requiring one tool per item type.

The server documentation describes guidance tools that return the current authoring specification and format-specific skill text. Miro presents these as agent-facing instructions with prescribed call order.
OAuth team selection creates a documented one-team-at-a-time connection per user, including across multiple clients; reauthorizing another team supersedes the earlier connection.
Miro's public client repository distributes agent skills alongside MCP configuration, but those skills are not the hosted server's source code.
